entities.name: Polyxenidas
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Polyxenidas the Rhodian, an exiled general and admiral, rose to prominence as a key military figure in the service of the Seleucid monarch Antiochus III the Great during the pivotal Seleucid-Roman War (192–188 BCE). His career, spanning the early 2nd century BCE, epitomized the fluidity of allegiance and the strategic importance of naval power in the Hellenistic world, as he commanded significant fleets against both Rhodes and the ascendant Roman Republic. His tactical acumen, though ultimately insufficient to stem the tide of Roman expansion, made him a formidable opponent whose actions profoundly influenced the balance of power in the Aegean Sea.

Polyxenidas's most notable engagements include the Battle of the Eurymedon in 190 BCE, where he achieved a significant, albeit temporary, naval victory over a Rhodian fleet under the command of Pausistratus near Side, demonstrating his mastery of Hellenistic naval tactics. However, this success was overshadowed by his decisive defeat at the Battle of Myonessus later the same year against a combined Roman and Rhodian fleet led by Lucius Aemilius Regillus and Eudamus. This catastrophic loss effectively crippled the Seleucid navy, granting Rome undisputed control of the Aegean and disrupting Antiochus III's ability to reinforce his land forces in Anatolia. His subsequent actions included a prolonged, unsuccessful siege of Notium, further highlighting the dwindling Seleucid strategic options.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Polyxenidas's naval command, particularly his defeat at Myonessus, directly contributed to the destruction of the Seleucid fleet, decisively shifting naval power in the Eastern Mediterranean to Rome and accelerating the end of Hellenistic independence.
